title: Where does range stop?
code:
total = 0
for n in range(1, 4):
    total += n
print(total)
explanation: range(1, 4) yields 1, 2 and 3. The stop value is excluded.
hint: The final value in the loop is 3.

title: A valid zero
code:
const count = 0;
console.log(count ?? 10);
explanation: Nullish coalescing uses the fallback only for null or undefined. Zero is retained.
hint: Compare ?? with ||.

title: A zero gets replaced
code:

explanation: || replaces all falsy values. ?? preserves zero and falls back only for null or undefined.

title: Build a two-column layout
code:
.stage { min-height:240px; }
.card { padding:24px; background:#fff; border-radius:16px; }
solution:
.stage { min-height:240px; display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr; gap:16px; background:#edf2e6; }
.card { padding:24px; background:#fff; border-radius:16px; }
goal: Make the stage a grid with two equal columns and a 16px gap.
explanation: Make the stage a grid with two equal columns and a 16px gap. These checks verify layout properties, not a pixel-perfect score.
hint: Inspect display, alignment, columns and gap on .stage.

title: Make a flexible row
code:

.card { min-width:120px; padding:24px; background:#fff; }
solution:

.card { min-width:120px; padding:24px; background:#fff; border-radius:16px; }
goal: Use a wrapping flex row with a 12px gap so cards can fit on narrow screens.
explanation: Use a wrapping flex row with a 12px gap so cards can fit on narrow screens. These checks verify layout properties, not a pixel-perfect score.
hint: Inspect display, alignment, columns and gap on .stage.

title: Total each customer’s orders
